items.title: Plea before Delhi High Court alleges gender disparity in Territorial Army officers' recruitment
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday issued notice to the Central government on a plea challenging the policy allocating a substantially higher number of Territorial Army (TA) officer vacancies to men while restricting women candidates to a single seat [Kush Kalra v Union of India & Ors] . A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia directed the government to file its reply to the plea. The petition was filed by Kush Kalra, arguing that in recruitments since 2022, only one seat has been given to women in the Territorial Army. It was stated that the 2022 recruitment had 12 vacancies for men and one for women, while the corresponding figures were 18 and one in 2023 and 2025. The 2026 recruitment provided 11 vacancies for men and one for women. Kalra argued that this practice was violative of Articles 14, 15 and 16 of the Constitution since the allocation effectively undermines the 2018 judgment of the High Court which paved the way for women's entry into the Territorial Army. items.title: SFI moves Delhi High Court over suspension of Instagram account
items.summary: Student’s Federation of India (SFI) has approached the Delhi High Court challenging the alleged delay by the Central government’s grievance appellate committee (GAC) in deciding its appeal against Instagram’s permanent disabling of one its accounts. Justice Amit Mahajan is scheduled to hear the case on September 24. SFI is the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist). According to SFI, Instagram permanently disabled the SFI Delhi account on July 5, stating that it “may be associated with another account that has gone against our rules” and therefore did not comply with its community standards on account integrity. SFI states that Instagram did not disclose any further particulars or identify the allegedly associated account. The account, created in 2018, had around 13,000 followers. The petitioners said they first appealed the disabling on July 7 and subsequently approached Meta's grievance officer on July 9. However, they received no response, following which they approached the GAC on August 12. As of September 16, the GAC website showed the appeal as “under process”, despite more than 30 days having elapsed, the petition stated. The petitioner has relied on Rule 3A

items.title: Distribute samosas and tea to DHCBA employees: Delhi High Court to lawyers as condition to waive costs
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently directed counsel for a litigant to distribute chai and samosa to Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA) employees as condition to do away with costs imposed by it earlier. In an order passed on September 17, Justice Saurabh Banerjee directed the lawyers for the petitioner to comply with the direction within one week. "The present application is disposed of, however, learned counsel for the petitioners is called upon to distribute samosas and tea to all the employees of Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA) within a period of one week." Justice Saurabh Banerjee and Delhi High Court The matter pertained to cheque bounce case against the petitioner company, Indus Birra Beverages and its officials. The company was seeking quashing of the criminal complaint under Negotiable Instruments Act. On August 20, the Court had dismissed the petition and imposed costs of ₹50,000 on the petitioers for not making full disclosure of a trial court order. They then filed an application to waive the costs. The Court allowed the same on September 17 subject to the lawyers distributing tea and samosas to DHCBA employees. items.title: Supreme Court takes suo motu cognisance of Patna HC ruling that removing woman's salwar, pressing chest not rape attempt
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday took suo motu cognisance of a Patna High Court ruling which held that removing a woman’s salwar and pressing her chest is not sufficient to establish the offence of attempt to rape. [In Re: Order dated 09.07.2026 passed by the High Court of Judicature at Patna in Criminal Appeal (SJ) No. 775/2013 and Ancillary Issues] A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the High Court judgment contained “offending observations”. “ There are some offending observations in the judgment. We will be able to set aside these only after hearing the accused. Issue notice to Himanshu Pathak. We request AG SD Sanjay for the State of Bihar to effect service on the contesting respondent through the local police. Post this matter for further consideration, ” the Court said. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Patna High Court made the observations on July 9 while setting aside accused Himanshu Pathak’s conviction for attempt to rape in a 2008 case. items.title: Punjab & Haryana HC seeks explanation from judge for wrongly attributing district court order to High Court
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court recently sought an explanation from an additional district judge for mistakenly writing that the High Court had stayed proceedings in an application moved by Punjab State Warehousing Corporation for execution of an arbitration award [Hardev Singh and Ors v Punjab State Warehousing Corporation and Anr] The Court was informed that the order staying the operation of the award was actually passed by an additional district judge in Chandigarh who is hearing a challenge against the award. Justice Lapita Banerji called it a serious issue and sought a report from the district judge of Muktsar Sahib. "Let a status report be called from the learned District Judge, Sri Muktsar Sahib, explaining the anomaly that has crept into the order dated August 19, 2026, passed in EXE-86-2024. It is also to be explained how despite recording that the presence of the decree holder is awaited the appearance of the learned counsel for the decree holder is recorded and how after recording that the JDs No. 1 to 7 are proceeded against “ex parte”, the learned ADJ recorded the presence of the learned counsel for JDs No.3 to 6," the Court said. items.title: Bedbugs in railway station VIP sofas: Court issues contempt notice to Divisional Railway Manager
items.summary: A railway court at Aurangabad has issued a show cause notice to the Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) of Nanded division over bedbug infested sofas in the VIP room at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar railway station. Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) SM Aher warned the senior official of contempt of court proceedings for failing to address the issue despite earlier directions. The matter arose in May 2026 when Justice Manjusha Deshpande of Bombay High Court and her husband noticed old, pest-infested sofas in the VIP room and reported the matter. Justice Manjusha Ajay Deshpande On May 20, Magistrate Aher directed the DRM to carry out pest control and replace the old sofas so that inconvenience is not caused to the judges. However, railway authorities failed to take action or respond for nearly four months. In the show cause notice of September 19, the Court noted that judges are now forced to wait in their vehicles instead of using the designated lounge. “As the sofas in VIP room are having bed bugs, this is very disgusting position to sit on those sofas by Hon'ble High Court Judges i.e. very very important persons and they are now sitting in their cars instead of sitting in VIP room,”
